key_insight: Inverse PINNs can estimate Manning friction reliably in some shallow-water settings, but success depends strongly on geometry, observation density, noise, and whether both depth and velocity are observed.
engineering_relevance: This benchmark helps engineers judge when sparse-field data are sufficient for calibrating hydrodynamic models and when inverse PINN friction estimates are likely to be biased or unreliable.
method: Train a PINN jointly for the flow field and a positive scalar Manning coefficient.
Use a two-phase strategy: fit observations first, then add the physics residual.
Benchmark recovery under varying sparsity, noise, and observed variable types in 1D and 2D shallow-water cases.
evidence_signal: In 2D, friction error stayed below 5% with at least 10 depth and velocity observations at noise levels up to 10%, while the 1D case showed a persistent ~15% positive bias regardless of data amount.
watch_item: The 1D benchmark suggests structural identifiability limits, so adding more sparse noisy data may not fix bias if the model setup cannot uniquely determine friction.
paper_title: How Sparse and How Noisy? Systematic Benchmarking of Inverse Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Manning Friction Estimation in Shallow Water Equations
